title: Wilson tells him about Louis Armstrong; he gives up trumpet and sax for piano
summary: Mr. Wilson sends him to Louis Armstrong, whom he hears with Erskine Tate in Chicago; he abandons trumpet, sees Hawkins make sax hopeless, and moves to piano.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Normal, Alabama, N-o-r-m-a-l. See because right out from that was the Seventh Day Adventists that later on a lot of peoples joined that. It's Huntsville, J.F. Drake, Alabama, they say, and later on Professor Jack (Tfadrick?) became the Professor. But Mr. James H. Wilson, he had been with the 24th and he had been with the 10th Cavalry and he was a flexible man. He was the one that told me about Louis Armstrong; but here's a man that's playing classical music, what does he know about Louis Armstrong? I knew about Charlie Charleston; I knew about Johnny Dunn but I -

Charlie Charleston played with a band out of Jackson, Tennessee, and he was born originally in St. Louis and I thought that he was the man and Johnny Dunn, but Mr. Wilson told me this is no, Louis Armstrong. I said, who is Louis Armstrong? So I had a distant cousin that took me back in Chicago and I went to see Mr. Louis Armstrong playing with Erskine Tate at the Vendome Theatre with that trumpet with the spotlight on him - I quickly gave up the trumpet. I thought I was going to play saxophone and later on in my years, in my formative years, having as a kid, dabbled around in shows, in Chautauqua shows, in carnivals and circuses and little gilly shows and what have you, I was in an advantage to travel. Then I was going to play

saxophone and here comes Coleman Hawkins, so forget it, so I switched to the piano. In 1930 Adelaide Hall came to Omaha, Nebraska. By that time I had migrated because I was going to continue my education, I thought, because I was with a band at the time called Skeet Morgan and R. C. Hicks and their Dixie Ramblers. We found ourselves out at Chillicothe, Missouri -
